'''Thomas Hansueli Zurbuchen''' (born 1968) is a Swiss-American [[astrophysicist]]. From October 2016<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://nasawatch.com/archives/2016/09/new-science-mis.html|title=NASAWatch article announcing Zurbuchen's NASA appointment|website=Nasawatch.com|date=27 September 2016 |access-date=2017-01-27}}</ref> until the end of 2022, he was the longest continually running Associate Administrator for the [[Science Mission Directorate]] at [[NASA]].<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://science.nasa.gov/about-us/leadership/Thomas-Zurbuchen|title=Thomas Zurbuchen bio at NASA|website=Science.nasa.gov|access-date=2017-01-27}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2022-09-14 |title=NASA's Science Associate Administrator Thomas Zurbuchen to Step Down |url=https://executivegov.com/2022/09/nasas-science-associate-administrator-thomas-zurbuchen-to-step-down/ |access-date=2023-01-26 |website=Executivegov.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Thomas Zurbuchen |url=https://nyce.org/thomas-zurbuchen |access-date=2026-10-26 |website=The New York Climate Exchange |language=en-US}}</ref> Prior to this, he was Professor of Space Science and [[Aerospace Engineering]] at the [[University of Michigan]], where he helped found the Center for Entrepreneurship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/12/science/thomas-zurbuchen-nasa-science.html|title=At NASA, Dr. Z Was OK With Some Missions Failing|first=Kenneth|last=Chang| date=January 12, 2023| access-date=13 January 2023|website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

Since 2023, Thomas Zurbuchen is a full professor at [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Thomas Zurbuchen {{!}} ETH Zürich |url=https://eaps.ethz.ch/personen/profil.thomas-zurbuchen.html |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Eaps.ethz.ch |language=de}}</ref><ref name="eaps.ethz.ch">{{Cite web |title=Weltraumwissenschaft und -technologie |url=https://eaps.ethz.ch/forschung/institute/geophysik/weltraum-wissenschaft-technologie.html |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Departement Erd- und Planetenwissenschaften |language=de}}</ref> where he leads the ETH Zürich | Space initiative<ref>{{Cite web |title=Contact |url=https://space.ethz.ch/contact/ |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Space.ethz.ch|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="eaps.ethz.ch"/> and has built the space systems master's degree programme.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Space Science and Technology |url=https://eaps.ethz.ch/en/research/institutes/geophysics/space-science-technology.html |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-17 |title=Launch of space systems degree programme |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2024/12/globe-launch-of-space-systems-degree-programme.html |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=ETH Zurich |language=en}}</ref> He also does advisory engagements and keynote speaking.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thomas Zurbuchen |url=https://www.thomaszurbuchen.com/ |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Thomas Zurbuchen |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="Board of Directors">{{Cite web |title=Board of Directors |url=https://group.schindler.com/en/company/corporate-governance/board-of-directors |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Group.schindler.com|language=en}}</ref>

Since October 2026, he serves as Senior Vice President of Advanced Concepts at [[Blue Origin]].

In 2021 an asteroid was named after Zurbuchen.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wise |first=Derek |date=2021-09-21 |title=Asteroid named for NASA Science Mission Directorate Associate Administrator Thomas Zurbuchen |url=https://spaceexplored.com/2021/09/21/asteroid-named-for-nasa-science-mission-directorate-associate-administrator-thomas-zurbuchen/ |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Spaceexplored.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life and education ==
Zurbuchen was born and grew up in Switzerland as the child of a Free Church preacher.<ref name="youtube.com">{{Cite web|via=[[YouTube]]|title=Aus der Freikirche ins All – Die steile Karriere des Nasa-Direktors Thomas Zurbuchen {{!}} Doku{{!}} SRF Dok | date=21 February 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2pov_bBZbxc |access-date=2023-05-03 |language=en}}</ref> He attended both high school and university against the wishes of his parents.<ref name="youtube.com"/> Zurbuchen studied [[physics]] at the [[University of Bern]], with a minor in [[mathematics]], and was awarded a PhD in 1996 with a thesis entitled "Turbulence in the interplanetary medium and its implications on the dynamics of minor ions".<ref>{{cite report|title=Astrophysics Data System reference for Zurbuchen's thesis | bibcode=1996PhDT........34Z| last1=Zurbuchen| first1=Thomas| year=1996}}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:NHQ201709050001~large.jpg|thumb|Zurbuchen gives opening remarks at an event to celebrate the 40th Anniversary of the launch of the [[Voyager mission]]s, September 5, 2017]]

Zurbuchen moved to the United States two weeks after completing his PhD.<ref name="zurbuchen20230525">{{Cite web |last=Zurbuchen |first=Thomas |date=2023-05-25 |title=Thomas Zurbuchen - The Next Step, Across The Atlantic, As An Immigrant |url=https://spaceref.com/science-and-exploration/thomas-zurbuchen-next-step-across-atlantic-immigrant/ |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=Spaceref.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He joined the [[University of Michigan]] as a [[research associate]], and was made professor in 2008. His scientific research focuses on solar and heliospheric physics, experimental space research, and space systems; he is also well known for his personal work on innovation and entrepreneurship.<ref>{{cite web |title=About Me |url=https://blogs.nasa.gov/drthomasz/about-me/ |access-date=19 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240530164059/https://blogs.nasa.gov/drthomasz/about-me/ |archive-date=30 May 2024}}</ref>

Zurbuchen served as team leader for the development of one of the scientific instruments aboard NASA's [[Messenger spacecraft]] to [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], the Fast Imaging Plasma Spectrometer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sprl.umich.edu/projects/FIPS/|title=FIPS Page at University of Michigan|access-date=2017-01-27}}</ref> He chaired the [[National Academy of Sciences]] committee that produced a report in 2016 on [[Cubesat]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sites.nationalacademies.org/SSB/CurrentProjects/SSB_160539|title=Achieving Science with CubeSats: Thinking Inside the Box (2016)|website=Sites.nationalacademies.org|access-date=2017-01-17}}</ref>

From October 2016<ref name=":0" /> until the end of 2022, Zurbuchen was the longest continually running Associate Administrator for the [[Science Mission Directorate]] at [[NASA]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name="auto"/> During this time, NASA launched 37 missions and started another 54.<ref name="Thomas Zurbuchen">{{Cite web |title=Thomas Zurbuchen |url=https://www.thomaszurbuchen.com/ |access-date=2023-01-26 |website=Thomaszurbuchen.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":2"/> Among them were the [[James Webb Space Telescope]], [[Perseverance (rover)|Perseverance]] and [[Ingenuity (helicopter)|Ingenuity]] Mars Landings, [[Demonstration for Autonomous Rendezvous Technology|DART]], and many others for which he was responsible, and for his contribution to the success of which he was awarded the von Braun Award for Excellence in Space Program Management.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-27 |title=Award for space researcher Thomas Zurbuchen |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2025/06/award-for-space-researcher-thomas-zurbuchen.html |access-date=2026-10-26 |website=Ethz.ch|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Launching the World's Biggest Space Telescope – Dr. Thomas Z |url=https://blogs.nasa.gov/drthomasz/2021/08/02/launching-the-worlds-biggest-space-telescope/ |access-date=2023-01-26 |website=Blogs.nasa.gov |date=2 August 2021 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2"/> Due to his work, Zurbuchen is routinely featured in interviews, public lectures, and podcasts, focussed on leadership innovation and management techniques, especially in complex organizations. Examples include, but are not limited to the Harvard Business Review,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-10-18 |title=NASA's Science Head on Leading Space Missions with Risk of Spectacular Failure |work=Harvard Business Review |url=https://hbr.org/podcast/2022/10/nasas-science-head-on-leading-space-missions-with-risk-of-spectacular-failure |access-date=2023-05-03 |issn=0017-8012}}</ref> the Knowledge Project,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thomas Zurbuchen: Adventures in Astrophysics [The Knowledge Project Ep. #108] |url=https://fs.blog/knowledge-project-podcast/thomas-zurbuchen/ |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=Farnam Street |language=en-US}}</ref> (German) Chefgespräch,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Balzli |first=Beat |title=Podcast – Chefgespräch: NASA-Forschungschef Zurbuchen: "Ende der 2030er Jahre werden wir auf de |url=https://www.wiwo.de/podcast/chefgespraech/podcast-chefgespraech-nasa-forschungschef-zurbuchen-ende-der-2030er-jahre-werden-wir-auf-dem-mars-landen/28873108.html |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=Wiwo.de |date=23 December 2022 |language=de}}</ref> and (German) Alles Gesagt.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ZEIT ONLINE {{!}} Lesen Sie zeit.de mit Werbung oder im PUR-Abo. Sie haben die Wahl. |url=https://www.zeit.de/zustimmung?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.zeit.de%2Fwissen%2F2022-07%2Fthomas-zurbuchen-alles-gesagt-interviewpodcast%3Futm_referrer%3Dhttps%3A%2F%2Fkeyboard-chartreuse-49xg.squarespace.com%2F |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=Zeit.de}}</ref>

As of January 2023, Zurbuchen works as an international speaker.<ref name="Thomas Zurbuchen"/><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 1, 2023 |title=LinkedIn: Thomas Zurbuchen |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/zurbuchen/ |website=Linkedin.com}}</ref> Since August 2023, Zurbuchen is director of [[ETH Zurich]] Space<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-25 |title=Former NASA Science Director is joining ETH Zurich |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2023/05/former-nasa-science-director-is-joining-eth-zurich.html |access-date=2023-05-25 |website=Ethz.ch |language=en}}</ref> and holds a full professorship there.<ref name="eaps.ethz.ch"/>
